markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (58%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs Benign · Careful review
Normal is in the 90% conformal set; invasive probability is under 1% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 58%, Normal 42% | Close call |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90%) | Cannot separate them |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.89 / 64th percentile | Input looks typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Split; three Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 1, 2, 11) · ↓ invasive · Largest concept term; spot check 0/20 · Unreliable
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 3, 9, 10) · ↓ invasive · Spot check 20/20 · Validated
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 0, 2, 8) · ↑ invasive · Concept model links it to invasion; spot check 19/20 · Validated
- **Immune cell fraction** (regions 3, 8, 11) · context · Higher than 96% of reference images [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions cuts the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion difference 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Normal and Benign overlap; the model cannot separate them at 90% coverage.
- Cell counts come from three regions with too few tumor nuclei to judge.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 2, 11:** Confirm normal lobules with two-layered epithelium; this concept failed its spot check.
2. **Regions 0, 2, 8:** Look for true stromal invasion versus reactive stroma.
3. **Regions 3, 8, 11:** Assess dense immune and dead cells for inflammatory background versus tumor.
